@graph.definition: Containment walls are constructed, usually in a series of stages, in a hybrid of upstream and downstream building methods. Construction begins with a starter dam, which forms the foundation for subsequent levels as the dam is raised. The dam wall remains fixed relative to upstream and downstream directions as the dam is sequentially built.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: Containment walls are constructed, usually in a series of stages, in a downstream direction. Construction begins with a starter dam which forms the foundation for subsequent levels as the dam is raised. Each new dam level built on and supported by on the outside or ‘downstream’ slope of the previous dam wall.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: Tailings that have been dewatered to below saturation point and, typically, deposited in piles to form a dense and stable ‘dry-stack’. Typically used to return water to the processing circuit, often recovering spent reagents or chemicals for re-use in processing.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: A shallow dam or structure designed to maximise evaporation of water to concentrate dissolved salts.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: An open-cut mine backfilled with waste material. Dam walls may or may not be built around the edge to increase capacity.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: Excavated rock, clay or soil, deposited and shaped to resemble a natural landform such as a hill. Typically shaped to minimise erosion.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: A single-stage dam is built to full height in one stage with no further additions.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: Used where there is insufficient information available to determine the structure type.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: Containment walls are constructed, usually in a series of stages, in an upstream direction. Construction begins with a starter dam which forms the foundation for subsequent levels as the dam is raised. Each new dam level is built on the inside or ‘upstream’ of the previous dam wall.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type

@graph.definition: Rock excavated from a mine and deposited in engineered locations. Also known as mullock heaps, rock dumps and rock piles.
@graph.schemeLabel: Mineral Resources - Mining Waste Structure Type
